title: Find Minimum Diameter After Merging Two Trees
summary: Given two undirected trees with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1 and 0 to m-1, and edge lists for each, you must connect one node from the first tree to another node from the second tree with an edge.
statement: Given two undirected trees with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1 and 0 to m-1, and edge lists for each, you must connect one node from the first tree to another node from the second tree with an edge. The task is to find the minimum possible diameter of the resulting tree. The diameter of a tree is defined as the longest path between any two nodes.
constraints: Each edge list describes a possibly single-node undirected tree numbered consecutively from zero.
Add exactly one edge joining any node of the first tree to any node of the second.
Return the minimum possible diameter of the combined tree, measured in edges.
hints: Connecting a center of each tree minimizes the longest path that crosses the new edge.
Find each diameter with two BFS sweeps; its minimum eccentricity is ceil(diameter/2).
Original diameters remain lower bounds, and every cross path through connected centers is bounded by the sum of the two radii plus one.
editorial: Original diameters remain lower bounds, and every cross path through connected centers is bounded by the sum of the two radii plus one.

tests.explanation: Connecting centers produces diameter three; no connection can make either original diameter smaller.
Joining the two single nodes creates one edge, so the diameter is one.
